# Current release — 5.26.0 · Room to play


## 5.27 — Pinch and keep

Two fingers on the game world now control the actual camera zoom: spread to
zoom in, pinch inward to zoom out. The chosen 50–300% scale stays exact through
movement, rooms, dialogue and battles, and is remembered on this device.
Pinching does not become a move, interaction or attack; the existing route is
preserved while the gesture temporarily suspends travel. Touch controls and
HUD buttons keep their own multi-touch ownership. Display & motion includes
an accessible World zoom slider and an explicit Use automatic zoom reset.

Manual battle framing follows the selected living crew member. The camera
uses the gesture midpoint while zooming, and world taps keep using the same
inverse transform. A single touch still moves/interacts on release; mouse and
pen behavior is retained. See docs/verification/release-5.27.md for checks.

Exploration now reserves more of the scene for the travelling crew. Field
labels share a budget of two on narrow screens and three on wider screens.
Threats and the current interaction take priority; secondary categories use
distance and a small retention preference to reduce label changes. Labels
avoid actor faces and the visible field card. Story contacts can keep a small
diamond without a full nameplate. Building exteriors and their portal objects
share one identity, including after the world's cloned scene data is loaded.

The field handoff keeps its first complete sentence and direct Explore here,
Approach pack when relevant, and Continue route actions. Threat, rewards &
preparation opens the complete advice, reward hint and Crew setup action in
place. Keyboard disclosure activation stays separate from the game's Pause
shortcut. Earned victory receipts retain their complete reward and equipment
comparison flow.

Walking and running now hold a brief planted stance around the existing foot
contacts, with a smooth weight transfer between them. Walking settles longer
than running. The same directional frames, distance clock, footfall cadence,
maximum offsets and immediate movement response remain; reduced motion removes
the extra body offsets.

Eight existing patrols across chapters 1–3 have explicit local formation
profiles. Workshop, Refuge stores, Drainage passages and Bypass introduce
different guard, caller, mender and striker pairings; Security, Console room,
Rail bridge and River path retain their established rosters. The same selected
actors supply field silhouettes, the revealed encounter brief and fresh battle
creation. Existing interception, alarms, repair and marked attacks provide the
choices. Patrol count, tier and reward identity remain tied to their existing
encounter; authored special encounters and restored battles keep their owners.

Neutral landscape telemetry is quiet. Meaningful cover, local resonance and
wildlife pressure appear as short field cues, while Pause → Local landscape
provides the sampled values and their meaning. The underlying vegetation,
resonance and ecology calculations remain in the existing Living Atlas bridge.
The recovered Grass and Vista sources were checked against the prior campaign
integration; their provenance remains recorded with those releases.

See [the 5.26 release record](../../../docs/verification/release-5.26.md) and
[cross-session source audit](../../../development/reconciliation/cross-session-audit-5.26.md).

# Release 5.25.0

The Eternal Sword Pact reference session's original Vista package is reconciled
with the existing Canvas2D game. Its source notice, prototype, tests and recovery
identity remain in `development/reconciliation/sources/vista-presentation-v1`.
The live integration reuses bounded quality, damping and effect descriptors;
scene depth comes from actual floor masks and existing authored landmark foci.
No second scene, render loop, terrain authority or simulated combat is installed.

`vista-scene.js` provides outdoor value separation, real-tree ground shade and
crew silhouette separation. `vista-combat-feedback.js` shows directional physical
impacts and confirmed armor-break / Guard / evade results. Effects remain below
or outside essential actor and warning information; compatibility and steady
settings preserve result labels. Camera look-ahead follows actual displacement
through the existing framing chain; battle and dialogue compositions retain
control of the lens.

Fresh ordinary patrols opt into `encounterTempo:{version:1}`. Their first
role-specific action precedes optional tool pickup, with readable warning time.
The marker and consumed opening survive snapshots. Boss, origin, rival,
frontier, friendly, wild and objective encounter timing remains independently
owned. No extra XP, damage, HP or rewards are generated by presentation.

# Release 5.24.0

The play loop now connects a readable encounter, a responsive command, and a
usable reward. Visible creatures and repair stock explain a real threat or use,
an answer available to the travelling crew, and an honest payoff.

Choose Attack, Guard or an affordable technique while readiness gathers. One
visible order approaches a distant target across actual floor and executes once
when legal. Cancel, manual movement, another action, Pause and scene changes
clear it. Clicking clear ground in battle moves the selected companion. Optional
Auto attack uses the same approach; Wait and Active timing remain available.

Fresh encounters give ordinary strikes 2.6-tile reach and damaging Mako an
8-tile clear path. Enemies close distance between warnings and hold their aim
while the warning is active. Ordinary pounces use the same small circle for
painting and hit detection. Existing in-progress saves keep their previous
combat geometry until their next fresh encounter.

Victory receipts show real equipment and forging-material changes, named
comparisons, conditional hit/protection effects, and an Equip action for any
recruited hero. Ring slots remain explicit. Equipment changes revalidate the
actual owned item and occupied slot; they never grant a second reward. The
original receipt survives later equipping, forging, and salvage.

The 5.23 soundtrack and 5.22 environment corrections remain in the campaign.
See [the fun assessment and research](../../../development/reconciliation/fun-research-5.24.md)
and [release verification](../../../docs/verification/release-5.24.md).

# Previous soundtrack release — 5.23.0

The campaign score now selects finite performances from contextual programs
instead of routing most scenes to the same short RPG loop. Homes, archives,
workshops, shorelines, woodland and other regions have separate selections;
all seven origins have different opening recordings. Actual recording hashes
and melodic families drive recent-history avoidance, including across reloads.
Reference performances and complete concert works remain intentional selections.

Spacious pacing is the default: a piece finishes, the environment has a quiet
interval, and a different piece follows. Night and quiet rooms allow longer
rests. Pause → Settings provides Continuous, Ambience only and Next piece.
Pausing freezes both playback and rest time; cinema and full-screen overlays
resume the retained position instead of restarting the opening. Combat uses
its chapter-appropriate action recordings and returns to the field afterwards.

Per-recording gains attenuate delivered music toward −22 LUFS without boosting
quiet files. Fresh music volume is 42%, optional instrument coloration starts
off, and existing explicit preferences are retained. Dialogue ducks the score.
Ambience only silences score and optional adaptive music textures while keeping
environmental sound, voices and gameplay signals. No audio assets were added.

The 5.22 environment corrections and all reconciled campaign content remain.
See [music inventory and routing audit](../../../development/reconciliation/music-audit-5.23.md)
and [release verification](../../../docs/verification/release-5.23.md).

# Previous environment release — 5.22.0

Outdoor scenery now follows one composition plan. Trees, low planting and
regional props form small groups at the banks and actual places of work.
The plan compares the full painted silhouettes against paths, doors, buildings
and interaction courts. It no longer appends independent global scatter or
forces unrelated regional tools into neighbouring decoration slots.

Generated stables, gardens, repair stock and regional work now respect this
shared space. Town roads share branches; villagers route around building
ground while preserving doorway approaches. The dry burrow repair is drawn
as low earth and boards, and listening points use small floor probes. Both
graphics modes use the same building geometry; underground entrances stay
stairwells. The Ground system retains its numerical effects without adding a
second decorative grid over the authored terrain.

The starter home and Sable's remembered home have a clear entrance aisle,
wall-backed storage and complete bedroom, kitchen and dining groups. Their
furnishing identities, interactions and supplies are preserved. Old saved
positions in newly occupied furniture cells repair to a nearby safe landing.
The seven origin routes and all integrated 5.21 systems remain playable.

See [composition rules and measured comparisons](../../../docs/verification/outdoor-composition-5.22.md)
and [release verification](../../../docs/verification/release-5.22.md).

# Previous integration release — 5.21.0

The recovered Living Armory v3, Living Atlas v8, Living Grass v6, Ground Forge
production package and Acoustic World v4 now run inside the campaign. Gear is
available through **Gear** or **Pause → Living Armory**. **Pause → Mossback &
Bellrun** opens the rebuilt mount and relay activities. The Hydrophone and
listening actions are available in Pause. The Developer portal offers **Try
the combined content**, an isolated practice fixture with a finite kit.

Equipment uses actual campaign inventory, credits, victories, caches and hero
stats. Ground and vegetation use real scene collision/materials. Hydrophone
phases alter the numerical Atlas field and interfere. Audio follows accepted
campaign events. All new persistent state travels through the existing save
and import/export mechanisms; old saves initialize the extensions without
receiving prototype rewards. Same-lineage origin transitions preserve earned
state. Actual new tellings follow their existing legacy rules.

The 5.18.1 campaign and its 172-motif environment collection remain the base.
Four legacy PNG deliveries are now pixel-identical lossless WebP copies;
original PNGs and unused unclean motion sources remain in repository history
and the development source directories. The full reconciliation matrix and
limitations are in [the release record](../../../docs/SESSION_RECONCILIATION_5.21.md).

# Previous environment release — 5.18.1

Environment collection II adds **48 original painted pieces on six sheets**:
24 fitted wall details for homes, workshops and civic rooms; 16 window-bay,
roof and wall details; and eight age/exposure tree variations. The combined
environment inventory now contains 172 motifs, including the same two staged
props. All 48 new pieces are selected in the actual world.

The placement audit finds 432 wall details across 59 rooms, 74 architectural
placements in 25 buildings, and 445 new canopy selections within the unchanged
1,451 visible tree sites. These are world-wide potential placements, before
culling. The five specialist chapel rooms keep their existing walls. Doors,
window centers, collision geometry and journey-save fields remain unchanged.

New walls and trees support Standard and Compatibility. New facade/roof art
uses Standard's detailed building path; Compatibility retains its established
simplified facade treatment. The optional sheets do not block startup when
unavailable. Original PNGs, measured crops and exact-alpha delivery proofs are
preserved with the source.

The Collection II gallery offers artwork and in-world scales, transparency and
traveller references. The Environment studio's **New detail** control visits
new placements in the production renderer without reading or writing journey
saves. Both are linked from the developer portal.

This art release extends the published 5.18 campaign. The unfinished Bellrun
5.19 work and the separate grass, ground and audio research retain their own
integration passes. The [session handoff](../../../docs/SESSION_RECONCILIATION_5.18.1.md)
records what the next campaign merge must preserve.

See [Environment art 5.18.1](../../../docs/ENVIRONMENT_ART_5.18.1.md),
[release verification](../../../docs/verification/release-5.18.1.md), and the
[next art briefs](../../../development/art/NEXT-ART-BRIEFS.md).

# Previous environment release — 5.18

A focused environment art expansion adds 124 original motifs and materials
across 16 new sheets: 96 props and shelter motifs, eight tree canopies, eight
ground surfaces, four water surfaces, and eight architectural accents. Two
props remain prepared for real authored placements; the other 122 motifs have
runtime mappings. The existing campaign and quality work are retained.

and materials. Both are linked from the developer portal.

# Previous exploration release — 5.15

Outdoor exploration now uses a small camera window that keeps scenery steady
during short movements while retaining existing composition and zoom. Ground
contacts are emitted at every crossed foot plant and placed along the actual
movement segment, including when a slow update skips the landing pose. The
Movement studio offers **Stable window** and **Centered follow** for comparison
and uses a correctly classified outdoor fixture.

The recorded full suite passes **872 tests across 118 modules**, with zero
failures or skips. See the [5.15 verification record](../../../docs/verification/release-5.15.md)
for the method, coverage, browser status and limits. The
[classic source study](../../../docs/CLASSIC_ENGINE_STUDY.md) documents public DKC
and Mana reconstructions used as engineering references. This release contains
original JavaScript changes; no reference-game code or assets were imported.
Existing movement speeds, artwork, combat rules and save format are preserved.

## Historical release notes

Current exploration release 2.4: 24 optional furnished interiors, 72 hidden caches, persistent keepsakes, and safe early workshop patrol gating. Six new original Gen2 cues were conditioned by aggregate features of ten CC0 game recordings. Those ten credited reference recordings are also playable at interior instruments. All enhanced-engine audio passes through an optional four-string modal bank tuned by the recovered Gen2 solver. This is a digital approximation, not measured hydrophone audio. 38 engine tests and two 24-chapter engine traversals pass. Browser save-import verification was interrupted; no physical-phone performance claim.

# Mako engine expansion — 2.3.0

The main /game/ entry now uses this original Canvas renderer and battle engine. /game/classic.html preserves the merged 1.2.0 SNES edition with separate saves and its exact original native patch. This is a browser engine expansion around the existing 24 chapter campaign, not a modified SNES ROM with larger graphics. The two save formats are intentionally separate; neither is silently converted.

The connected Stolen Song content pass (919b19c) and its independent audit ancestor are merged in authoring history. Its campaign authoring files and compiler fields are retained. world.json exports all 44 authored field/service scenes plus a workshop hub; it retains quest flags, early rescue consequences, named routes, chapter rewards and the ending. One disconnected passages mechanism gets a generated walkable connection. The exporter decodes collision only, not original graphics. Regenerate using `python game/engine2/export_world.py ORIGINAL_ROM`.

Art: seven crew rows with eight poses; six creature rows with four poses; four terrain families. art/manifest.json records original generated production briefs and hashes. Runtime crops, floor coverage, depth sorting, lighting, telegraphs and effects are engine code; no generated art is attributed to a historical game's artist.

Gameplay: ten cores times twelve supports compile 120 combinations (not 120 hand-animated authored attacks), with AP mastery, affinities, overdraw and strain, interruption, fields, echoes, elemental interaction, counters and two/three-person links. The 56 personal technique names and unlock masks use these effects. Enemies have six visual archetypes; ordinary guard/scout/mender/predator roles and eight chapter-dependent guardian patterns. Late guardians share art and behavior families; this does not claim 24 unique creature atlases.

Music uses the existing 57-entry catalogue and scene music mapping, including recovered Dyletsky performances. These are recorded/sampled cues, not a live physical instrument or a newly ported native generator. The diegetic listening kiln cycles through all 51 distinct recording assets, and chapter clears/debriefs use their authored cues. Music crossfades; battle effects are synthesized Web Audio. No external music dashboard is required.

Controls: keyboard, standard gamepad, eight-way touch joystick, face buttons and collision-aware tap paths. Manual movement cancels a tap path. Enemy taps select targets in combat. Equipment menus pause play. Save/Load, export/import and in-battle serialized delayed effects are supported. A previous enhanced save is retained when starting over; native saves are untouched.

Validation: `node --test game/engine2/tests/runtime.test.mjs` checks 120 recipes, costs, links, enemy AI, interruptions, wet/volt, counters, delayed/field save restoration, target geometry, reachable mechanisms, opening repair/theft/hatch, 24 reward transitions and 24 legally commanded simulated boss battles. These are model checks, not a controller-earned full campaign playthrough. Browser QA covers New Game intro, keyboard interaction, tap movement, Mako equipment, continuation, and a deliberately imported isolated battle fixture followed by normal commands. Device hardware and a fresh continuous full playthrough remain unverified.

Performance: viewport culling, bounded effects, device pixel ratio capped at 1.5, HUD updates at ~6 Hz, cached decoded atlases. A sampled desktop browser drawing average was ~1 ms; this is not a mobile device FPS guarantee.

## Presentation polish — 2.1.0

New generated run art is saved as `art/crew-run-v2.png`; built-in image_gen, its production prompt set, reference and hash are recorded in `art/manifest.json`. The existing sheet retains idle and combat poses. Each actor now has independent facing and a four-phase, distance-driven gait, including rear views and horizontal mirroring. Feet share a ground anchor, sprites preserve their source aspect ratio, and the party follows a recorded leader trail around corners. Stopping holds direction; finishing combat clears stale attack poses. Buildings are over three times crew height, the child is smaller than adults, and scenery uses coherent size constants in presentation.js. The opening orchestra is a code-rendered string/water instrument instead of a duplicate Rook or a generic shrine.

Text reflows native hard wraps, speaker names and page counters are visible, and portrait images retain their proportions. Compact exploration health cards expand during battle. Dialogue, spells, command panels and camera framing reserve space for touch controls; portrait and landscape have separate layouts and safe-area padding. The eight-way stick uses a centred knob and a smaller footprint; action buttons show their current role. Controls override tap paths cleanly, and empty released input sources are removed rather than accumulating. Stable HUD buttons replace per-frame button reconstruction. Menu focus is retained for keyboard/controller selection. Existing enhanced saves continue using the same schema and key.

Rook and Nell have explicit opening objectives; tapping an objective follows a collision-aware route and interacts on arrival. NPC names and exits are labelled nearby, blocked town terrain reads as water channels, sprite-body taps select the intended object, and failed ground paths report that they are unreachable. Finite beam hit geometry now matches its displayed warning, and circular warning radii match actual hit radii.

Validation: 23 engine/presentation model tests pass, plus the existing input-ui tests. Browser QA checked the real entry at desktop size and in 390x780 and 844x390 CSS viewports. It verified New Game, intro text, repair choice, objective progression, independent moving/idle actor metadata, joystick cancellation of an active tap route and return to centre, walking to Nell, choices, old-save Continue, no horizontal overflow at 390px, and dialogue/joypad separation in both phone orientations. These are desktop browser viewport checks, not physical Android hardware or a continuous full-campaign playthrough. The preserved 2.0 battle smoke scope remains in the prior receipts.

## Earned beginning — 2.3.0

New Game starts at the Lower Road home with only Sable, zero credits, no supplies, no learned personal techniques, no core patterns or linked slots, and new unarmored courier art. Mara’s parcel supplies two Tonics. The repaired orchestra earns 20 credits. Rook explicitly chooses to join after witnessing the theft; the workshop provides basic tools and then Earth/Focus. Iona is encountered as the prison medic, and her accepted recruitment supplies the first healing pattern. You cannot enter the yard without the tools and reader or begin its guardian rescue without her. Later companions still join through their authored chapters, with a clear message and journal entry.

The authored reward schedule is in opening.js: the first guardian yields a reinforced coat, Flame, Break and a second socket; Link follows the third chapter, a third socket the sixth. All ten core patterns and twelve supports become available through specific early-campaign milestones. Random cache core grants are disabled for this new progression. Rewards and recruitment supplies are once-only; the first guardian has been simulated successfully using only the actually earned opening loadouts. Legacy enhanced saves retain their old crew and equipment rather than losing progress. New Game is required to experience the revised beginning. The classic SNES edition is unchanged.

The journal records the delivery promise, companion motivations, discoveries, actual chapter debriefs and retry context. New original recording interludes in chapters 5, 15 and 21 lead to two final choices about the song; both return the reed case to Mara. Chapter 15 visibly removes Sable’s uniform. The two complete ending transitions are model-tested, not claimed as a new controller-earned full campaign run.

research/sources.json contains eight source-attributed records across six reference games, with coverage and limitations. research/campaign-integration.json maps the existing 24 chapters into the implementation and states the next playtest hypotheses. research/FINDINGS.md separates sourced observations from our design judgments. No claim of an optimal or empirically addictive story is made: appeal and voluntary return still need player testing.

New project assets, their built-in generation briefs and hashes are in art/manifest.json: art/sable-starter.png and art/home-interior.png. Runtime source cropping preserves proportions and alpha. Home furniture occupies blocked cells so the reed route remains walkable. The browser pass verifies the real New Game at phone CSS size, a single party card, locked Mako, civilian art, the home objective and Mara’s first earned item dialogue. It does not substitute a prepared save for that check.

## Integrated independent content pass — 2.2.0

The complete campaign overlay and latest engine polish are merged through Git history, including engine receipt 8d85cb1. Renderer, battle logic, Mako implementation and generated art match that engine receipt. Content changes belong to campaign-content.js, World progression, the collision exporter and authored campaign files. The main Canvas game remains the entry point; classic is a separate edition.

All 24 chapters have a goal, a discovery and a next lead, with at least two authored rooms per chapter. Seventeen interiors extend the original 44-room campaign to 61 rooms. Evidence, rescue, phrase and project requirements are actual progression gates. Seven decisions accept either answer; later supplies, optional routes and ending pages read the recorded choice. New causal goals appear in the HUD and journal. The objective button follows the first available passage toward the task, rather than suggesting a locked guardian.

Enhanced saves keep the existing schema and storage key. Existing crew, loadouts, AP, strain, inventory and completed guardians survive. Unrecorded choices stay unknown; migration does not invent the rejected or second option. Old players can revisit missing decisions, receive deferred conditional rewards and collect newly earned cache bonuses once. Old base loot and guardian rewards cannot be farmed through stale objects. Native snapshots remain separate and are never cast as enhanced saves.

Validation: 32 JavaScript checks cover existing combat/presentation and new choice, migration, one-shot reward, door, lift and journal behavior. qa/campaign-play.mjs runs both all-first and all-second choice paths through all 24 chapters, 66 actual Battle resolutions and 57 visited scenes each. It starts New Game, walks collision paths, uses authored interactions, earns levels/AP and pays technique and supply costs. It does not set quest flags, grant levels or force victories. It bypasses DOM/input scheduling and is engine-level evidence, not a full browser/controller playthrough; optional service rooms account for the remaining scenes. Unit geometry checks cover all 62 scenes including the hub. The two complete runs are not a claim that all 128 combinations received full playthroughs.

The original audit and its six-chain reference model are historical design evidence, not an assertion that every proposal in that model ships unchanged. Current source of truth is the 1.3.0 authored overlay plus this Canvas adapter. This remains smaller and more repetitive than Chrono Trigger: reused scenery and guardian families, limited optional quest arcs and no New Game Plus. The release fixes disconnected progression and shallow decision gates; it does not claim original-game parity or mobile performance certification.

The earned opening is integrated with this content pass: symbolic story choices, conditional rewards, migrated unknown choices, discovery log, causal navigation, expanded rooms and native/classic assets are retained. The new recording decision appends rather than replaces the full-arc choice epilogues.

### Exit and town wayfinding correction

All scene doors and portal objects now render a destination sign and an illuminated arch, gate, or stair/hatch at the real switching coordinate. Portal rendering takes priority over dialogue speaker inference. Town, market, and hub paving is compiled once per scene from a breadth-first tree of actual walkable cells connecting doors and activity anchors; activity medallions, brick roads, planters and lanterns distinguish the street network. Walkability, quest conditions and saved progress are preserved. Browser visual QA covered home exits and the town service-hatch/home routes through a temporary renderer harness; it was removed before publication. The 34 Node tests pass, including collision-respecting paving and destination naming. This does not claim a fresh continuous campaign or physical-phone performance run.

### Environment diversity correction 2.3.3

Replaces the freestanding glowing exit arches with material-specific indoor doors, recessed stairs and open outdoor route markers. Eight generated village façades identify home, instrument works, guild, inn, clinic, carpenter, market and foundry entrances. Six environment identities select eight painted ground materials: village stone/gardens, woodland meadow/leaf litter, mountain rock/snow, riverbank shale, ruined limestone and industrial gravel. Nonwalkable exterior borders and the area beyond map bounds are rendered as environment scenery rather than a dark void; street edge curbs retain a visible collision boundary. Removes randomly repeated castle sprites. Clinic/crypt stone, workshop metal and inn/guild runner overlays distinguish indoor floors. Source assets are art/world-materials-v3.png and art/village-buildings-v3.png, generated with the built-in image tool from the material-atlas and distinct-village-façade briefs; original generation copies are retained in the task workspace. Browser checks covered town and woodland previews. Existing campaign and save behavior are retained; there is no claim that every character or combat animation was redesigned, or that device performance has been measured.

Combined integration: imported other-session authoring commit eda149b129c480af762c3c1b6aec12c6d1740be2 onto environment revision 9ac4482750d07e8eb65bbfda10d8183494395513. Preserved the eight painted materials, distinct façades and contextual exits; added six-layout optional-room baking, hidden cache rendering, 24 rooms, 72 secrets, keepsake journal, six rendered Dyletsky cues, ten CC0 reference tracks, digital string/water processing, pause controls and workshop patrol gate. All 41 Node tests pass; all six Ogg files are readable; browser boot reports 86 scenes and 72 caches. Music is digital synthesis/processing, not a recording of physical hydrophone hardware.

### Narrative and voice revision 2.5

The user-authorized rewrite supersedes the animation pass's previous verbatim freeze. All24 campaign chapters receive1,429 guarded prose-field changes (including mirrored exports), plus12 opening/memory passages. The revised causal spine begins with the reed-case promise, follows Nell's father's theft through the carriage and water-test evidence, treats the Crown victory as incomplete, confronts the crew's complicity and the mother's copied recording, then returns to Mara. Puzzle answers, rewards, flags, branch indices and scene coordinates remain unchanged. Source old/new patches and causal notes live under narrative-work/.

The game now displays one named speaker turn per page. Narration has no false generic speaker title; inventory, learning, party and control receipts appear in a separate status strip and do not enter the voice queue. Exact speaker/text matching binds recorded voices; no robotic browser-speech fallback is used. Voice playback cancels on page/choice/scene/pause/load/close, ducks music only while audio plays, and exposes replay/mute/volume controls. HUD task and district labels now identify the action and place instead of generic mechanisms and fields. The story read-through is /game/story/; the animation manifests are regenerated against the revised script.

Recorded speech is generated through the user's connected Runway account using distinct preset cast voices. All source strings and task IDs remain in the production manifests. Two provider-blocked lines remain subtitled rather than being silently rewritten to bypass the block. Final counts and media verification are recorded under story/verification.json after integration. A browser smoke test confirmed Mara's actual MP3 playing with its matching subtitle and replay button. This is not a complete continuous human campaign playthrough or a subjective audition of every recorded line.

### Film viewer 2.5.1

Title and Pause now open an optional modal film viewer with the recovered silent Orchard pilot and three existing motion studies. Playback, seeking, replay and close controls preserve campaign state; game input is blocked while the viewer is open. No proposed cast is forced into current quest events. The 399 recordings and two subtitle-only turns remain intact. Browser QA confirmed Orchard decoding, playback through its 10.041667-second ending, and return to the title. All 55 existing checks pass; mobile hardware and full-speed artistic acceptance remain pending.

### Sprite isolation and repertoire 2.7

Renderer and animated story now isolate the principal connected sprite within each atlas cell, preserving alpha edges and removing detached neighboring feet/heads. The 54 motion-study frames were separately extracted and normalized to a shared foot baseline; all three six-second preview videos were rebuilt and decoded. Original source sheets are preserved. This does not reconstruct anatomy missing or clipped in a source painting.

Twelve newly generated creature designs are padded and isolated using measured source rectangles. Regular encounters from chapter 2 use these designs, with twelve elder variants later in the campaign; elder strikes gain 10% power, switch line/circle geometry and use a longer windup. Existing named story bosses and chapter-one combat training are retained. New moves apply status only on telegraph hits. The motion workshop includes a twelve-creature limited-motion viewer.

The supply repertoire grows from three to 27 usable items. Each has a distinct ID, actual combat effect, price, chapter-based market availability and a dedicated painted icon for new items in the field guide. Six-item shop pages avoid a 27-choice conversation. Caches give one chapter-specific extra supply; each encounter gives one extra drop only once, recorded in the save. Existing bags migrate lazily without losing quantities or granting a starter kit. Supply opens a battle selection menu; Pause includes a read-only bag. New effects include cleanses, shields, haste, area recovery, armor break/interrupt, burns, wet, shock and slow. No-op uses cost nothing.

Validation: 65 Node checks, both campaign branches (24 chapters and 66 fights each), full decode of rebuilt motion previews. Browser QA covered main-game boot and upright Sable sprite, the field guide’s isolated creature silhouettes and item art. Engine traversal is not a full controller/browser campaign run or physical-phone performance certification.

### Journey cinema 2.8

Recovered Ash_Aether_Cinematic_Upgrade.zip contains a 73-second concept edit, eight three-panel art boards and its local camera-editing recipe. Its older proposed cast and editorial captions are not treated as current dialogue. The original concept film is available in Watch films with that provenance. Environmental vignettes are cropped from the boards for in-game arrivals and the voiced story viewer’s first eight chapters.

The local renderer development/build_journey_cinema.py produces 20 new 1280x720, 24-fps, 3.5-second clips: eight environmental arrivals and twelve canonical creature reveals. This is camera movement, compositing, fades and limited cutout motion; it does not claim newly rigged anatomical movement or lip sync. Clips are loaded on demand and are silent, keeping the existing game music as the underlying score.

Arrival films play once on entry to chapters 1–8 (chapter 1 starts at the security yard, not the civilian home). Optional interiors, save restoration and later chapters are excluded. First encounters feature one unseen creature per battle, with captions derived from the actual enemy’s move geometry, including elder variants. Battles and movement are held during playback. End, skip and failure return without granting rewards, changing quest flags or choosing dialogue branches. Seen-film and encountered-species metadata is lazily retained in existing saves; pending presentations cancel on load/new game. A Pause toggle disables automatic scenes.

Journey album replays visited destinations and encountered creatures; older saves recover already completed chapter arrivals without future spoilers. The existing Watch films menu remains independent.

Validation: all 69 Node checks pass; both engine campaign routes complete 24 chapters and 66 fights; all 20 new videos fully decode. Browser QA verified automatic arrival playback/end, creature playback/skip, tactical caption and preservation of fixture quest flags, inventory and credits using a temporary lifecycle harness removed before publication. A temporary shared-preview root change was resolved before the successful playback checks. This is not a continuous browser campaign or physical-phone benchmark.

### Furnished, navigable interiors 3.0

All 56 current interiors receive room-specific furnishings, readable architecture and physical furniture footprints. The current build has 1,765 individually reachable and selectable furniture placements, using 24 new painted designs. Homes, inns, clinics, libraries, guilds, workrooms, chapels, gardens and water rooms use different object sets; cistern pools remain pools. The inn gains bedroom partitions and the clinic gains privacy divisions, with real collision and reserved openings. Appliance caps avoid repeated kitchens in one room. Windows cast cached light across floors; rugs, warm timber and stone palettes distinguish the spaces. Previous random wall furniture and duplicate home stamps are suppressed.

Ordinary interior exits are consolidated at actual room boundaries; stairs and hatches remain explicit vertical passages. Matching incoming routes arrive inside the corresponding doorway. Navigation reserves routes to existing characters, quests, encounters, doors and new inspection points before allocating furniture, so furniture cannot close a required corridor. Each furnishing receives its own interaction anchor, and tapping its visible art targets that anchor.

Objects can be examined, cupboards and desks can be opened/closed, hearths can ease field strain, and clearly marked shared-supply compartments provide a single road remedy. Inspection and opened-compartment state are saved independently of quest flags. Legacy saves inside a new collision footprint move to the nearest walkable tile while retaining crew, supplies and progress.

Runtime room construction uses generated household-plans.js with per-room geometry signatures. Rebuild with node development/build_households.mjs. A changed source room falls back to the live collision-aware planner. Desktop fixture construction measured about 113 ms using compiled plans; this is not a phone benchmark. Only the current room floor is baked into a canvas; furniture uses shared atlas cutouts.

Validation includes all furnishing anchors and ordinary exit boundaries, one-time supply claims and save roundtrips, legacy position recovery, normal opening navigation to Mara and a working hearth interaction in the browser. A temporary room fixture was used to inspect the home, inn and clinic layouts and removed before publication. Both engine campaign routes reach all 24 chapters through 66 battles and 81 visited rooms. These engine routes do not constitute a full controller/browser campaign playthrough.

Combined integration reserves all 72 source/device/reward placements from the physical-lore system before adding furniture and protects their approach space. These reservations are part of geometry cache signatures. Existing town-life, adaptive music, Wayglass, skill grid, story-flow and cinematic changes are preserved. The combined engine suite passes 121 tests, including 24 physical artifact chains; older dropped objects in newly occupied cells move to nearby floor without changing ownership or completion state.
